evidence_note: Reception extents are not the antiquarian reconstruction and are not claimed to continue it.
note: Kept as an explicit non-relationship so the reception material cannot inherit the authority of the scholarship it borrows from.

evidence_note: The diocese is the administrative container of the Danubian provinces that carry the name.
note: One Dacia contains the other. Recorded so a reader meeting both in the same register does not have to guess which is which.

evidence_note: A Roman mint and a medieval Latin usage for Denmark share a string and nothing else.
note: Adjudicated explicitly, like every other pair across the Danube/Baltic divide, so that no reader has to decide for themselves whether the coin is evidence about Denmark.

evidence_note: The later province is named after the abandoned one by the same administration.
note: Derivation of the name only. This edge asserts nothing about the movement of people.

evidence_note: The civil diocese and the Danish usage are unrelated referents sharing a string.
note: Recorded for the same reason as the others: the Latin word is the only thing the two have in common.

evidence_note: Ortelius restores the ancient province from the authors in the Parergon of 1595.
note: A deliberate reach back across the gap, not an unbroken inheritance.

evidence_note: The mint strikes the name of the province the same administration had just made.
note: The same referent named by two arms of one state. It is not continuity, because no attestation has been cited to carry the claim.

evidence_note: The diocese south of the Danube is named from the province north of it by the same administration.
note: Derivation, not continuity: the ground is different ground, and the register that attests the diocese says nothing about the province it was named after.

evidence_note: Two unrelated referents share a string; no relationship is claimed.
note: The load-bearing edge of the trench: lexical identity here is a coincidence of transmission, and the corpus says so explicitly rather than leaving the reader to infer continuity from the word.

evidence_note: The church province takes its name from the geographic usage already current.
note: Both ends still need source review.

evidence_note: Re-attached by decree in 1974 after eighteen centuries of Klausenburg, Kolozsvar and Cluj.
note: The instrument is administrative, not linguistic: the name did not survive, it was reinstated.
